citations.claim: after first step speed ~0.94 due to controller force exceeding limit
controller_force at step 1 is 83.438 which exceeds limit 64.183 per violation detail

counterfactual.change: Set controller noise from 0.22834833654201386 to 0, leaving all other fields identical. This removes post-clamp noise amplification and makes force equal to fmax 64.183, so rule passes.

args.explanation: Controller uses velocity-error law F = kp*(v_desired - v_perceived). With sensor noise 0.228, perceived velocity is perturbed, increasing velocity error. The implementation applies noise after the fmax clamp (or adds noise to force/desired velocity with gain), so final commanded force 83.438 exceeds declared fmax 64.183. Counterfactual with noise=0 clamps exactly at fmax and passes, proving noise handling breaks force limiting.

description: In both tiles the red controller-driven body is on the right side of the arena and the green waypoint is to its left; the body shows almost no displacement between step 0 and step 1. There is no visible wall penetration, tunneling, or extreme motion – the controller_force_limit violation is in the commanded force, not in the positions.
